b: Once we get through today’s poem, we’ll be two thirds of the way through the challenge. Sooo…

For today’s prompt, write a response poem. Your poem could respond to anything: something you overheard at the grocery store, read in a magazine, watched on television, or experienced in real life. Respond to another poem (even one of your own). Give the counterpoint, or push the point even further, or change the mood (from happy to sad or vice versa).
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Response Poem:

We descend upon the coffee shop
like vampires after the sun descends,
and we snap fingers and hurl words
into the mic for our allotted time–
some in free verse, others in rhyme
(reading from our smart phones or
unfolded maps of manic manifestos)–
drinking our sweetened cappuccinos
getting inspired and inspiring as we
search (deeply) for the truest meanings
that can never quite be captured
(at least the way we feel it most)
by each poet or generous host.
(Note on my response poem: I decided to respond to my Day 16 group poem.)
